facts.fact: Freedom House reports the news site Cairo 24 was blocked in Egypt in November 2024 with no explanation from authorities, within a wider blocking of news websites by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation.

Freedom House reports the Brussels-based independent Egyptian outlet Zawia3 was blocked in Egypt in February 2025, within a wider blocking of news websites by the Supreme Council for Media Regulation.

Freedom House reports a long-standing ban on Voice over Internet Protocol services such as WhatsApp or Viber calling had not been lifted by the end of its coverage period, despite a late-2024 announcement by the telecom regulator NTRA of plans to lift it, and several VoIP services remained inaccessible; the document gives no date for this beyond its publication (2025-11-12).

Freedom House, citing Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch, reports more than 100 people were arbitrarily detained in June and July 2024 after using social media to call for protests over power cuts and rising prices.
facts.system: Detention of people who used social media to call for protests

facts.fact: Freedom House reports that in September 2024 authorities added two years to the five-year prison sentence of the prodemocracy blogger Alaa Abdel Fattah days before his scheduled release, as an example of internet users arrested for their online activity.

Alaa Abdel Fattah's September 2025 pardon is a release, not a penalty. Power outages and the Fakartany licence refusal are not cuts by order or are class other.
Monthly report on the Unified Government Complaints System (citizen service complaints); no criticism by a named outside body, no cut, no punishment for speech.

facts.fact: Al Manassa quotes Egyptian Journalists Syndicate head Khaled Elbalshy rejecting all blocking of news websites and the licensing justification for the regulator's move against Egyptke.
Al Manassa reports security forces arrested Egyptke's editor-in-chief and CEO in December 2025 after a complaint over a poultry story the complaint called falsely attributed.

note: The regulator's request to NTRA to block Egyptke is a request, not a reported block.

facts.fact: Access Now and co-signatories say Egyptian authorities continue to block independent media sites, with at least 630 websites currently blocked.

Human Rights Watch says Egyptian security forces arrested the six journalists of the Matsda2sh newsroom on 28-29 September 2026, and the Interior Ministry said they were suspected of preparing fabricated news.

The convictions are for content breaching family values, not stated to be about the government or public affairs; the criticism cited is of a law, not a named government decision.

facts.fact: LDSF reports content creators were arrested and sentenced in 2025, including Mohamed Abdel Aaty to two years on 29 November 2025, for charges of harming family values and misusing social media.

note: Document states nothing the study asks for this country.

facts.fact: UN News, citing the OHCHR spokesperson, reports that the six journalists of the fact-checking website Matsadash remained in detention on 10 November 2026, with OHCHR calling for charges arising from their journalistic work to be dropped.
UN News reports that in October 2026 an Egyptian court convicted Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah of operating an unlicensed website, fined her and ordered the website closed.
CPJ says Egypt has blocked outlets since 2017, most recently Zawia3, whose site is blocked inside Egypt.
CPJ says an in absentia conviction in 2024 sentenced Mada Masr's Lina Attalah to one year for disseminating false news and operating an unlicensed website.

note: The 27 October 2026 closure and fine of Mada Masr were for an unlicensed website, not stated as for what it published.

facts.fact: Al Manassa reports that on 27 October 2026 New Cairo Misdemeanor Court fined Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah EGP 3 million and ordered the news website closed, on charges of operating a website without a license.

The Egyptian Human Rights Forum report, via Al Manassa, says Al Manassa has been blocked 13 times, most recently in July 2022, and the Journalists Syndicate criticised the continued blocking in March 2024.

The Guardian reports that a Cairo court convicted Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah of managing an unlicensed website, she was held until a EGP 3 million fine was paid, and the court ordered the Mada Masr site shut; the outlet says it had applied for a licence three years earlier without reply.

note: The Matsadaash arrests are described here as charges of belonging to the Muslim Brotherhood, not speech.

facts.fact: Freedom House says Egyptian authorities blocked communications platforms in the coverage period as part of a crackdown on online mobilisation.

Freedom House says Egyptian authorities arrested people for joining political groups organised on social media, citing Amnesty International's July 2026 call to release dozens detained over a Gen Z online group.

note: Editors asked for state action on social media; no criticism of a named policy, cut or punishment is stated.

facts.fact: Journalists Syndicate deputy head Mohamed Saad Abdel Hafez said government and parliament had dragged their feet for 12 years in issuing the access to information law the 2014 constitution requires.

note: A bill on defamation and fabricated content is not a repeal, cut or named punishment.
